doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: What he wants students to master
summary: His criteria: time, tone and harmonic rhythm; he demonstrates at the piano.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Is there a short list of things that you really want your students to be able to do by the time they move on?
And what might be a couple of them?

Well play in time. Have a good tone. Play in time with the rhythm, not just rhythmically correct but the harmonic rhythm, the harmonic rhythm. That means like when you’re playing these standards or playing the modal stuff, you’re playing the harmony it has to have, the rhythm of the harmony has to resolve in the right places. Because there’s corny places to resolve, and there’s hip places to resolve. You know what I’m saying? So and not to get too into it, but that’s my criteria. You’ve got to learn how to do that, if you want to be my student. You know, and that’s great, they love it because now it starts to make sense what they’re playing.
What method do you use in a lesson? Do you play chords with them?

Sometimes. Sometimes I play on saxophone. If they don’t hear it I go to the piano and say you’re playing this note. I’ll play the chord and say, “Here’s the note you landed on.” And they say, “Oh yeah. Now I know what you mean by wrong and tension.” There it goes again.
